text:
aj: Heads up — after rolling a staged int4 quant for DDP-13b on staging, we're seeing a ~1.4% drop on the longform recall slice (priming-heavy). Cost savings look ~33%/token. Anyone else see this?

sara: I saw the same on the smoke runs. High variance on prompts with long system+context. Exact-match and recall both down on the tail.

liam: Can you paste the quick perf + cost numbers and the quant config? Also how much traffic was on staging? Might be a priming sensitivity.

aj: quick numbers: int8 baseline p@k (longform) 0.720, int4 0.706. Cost/token: int8 ~$0.00052, int6 ~$0.00042, int4 ~$0.00035 (approx). Latency delta negligible at median, tails slightly noisier. Traffic: 100% of the staging cohort (no traffic split yet). Quant config: q4_0 symmetric, global scale, no per-channel, no outlier-handling.

sara: Hypothesis: block-wise/global scale quant + kv-cache alignment for long prefixes is hurting primed examples. Two low-effort levers: 1) try int6 (or q6_k) for primed requests; 2) enable per-channel/scaled quant or outlier correction for int4. Also enable prefix KV caching for the int4 path if it isn't yet.

liam: Agree. Suggested playbook:
1) Run a targeted A/B on the priming slice (50/50 int4 vs int6) for 24h to get signal.
2) Parallel microbench: int4 with per-channel scale / outlier handling on the same slice.
3) If int6 recovers >0.5% p@k vs int4 at ~20% higher cost, consider hybrid routing (route priming-heavy requests to int6).

aj: Product question — for hybrid routing we'd need a lightweight signal (priming length or prompt tag). We can ship a flag but want to be explicit to GTN on expected cost/quality tradeoff. Example config I sketched:

```json
{
  "routing_flag": "hybrid_priming_int6",
  "selector": {"priming_tokens_gt": 512},
  "buckets": {"int6": 1.0, "int4": 4.0}
}
```

sara: Also try a cheap calibration run: quantize per-channel for embedding/attention layers only. In our past runs that recovers ~0.005-0.01 p@k with nearly zero cost delta. Worth trying before routing.

liam: I'll own the 24h A/B and the eval harness. Plan: kick off now, collect p@k, exact-match, latency tail, and token-econ. ETA mid-day tomorrow.

aj: Thanks. I'll draft a short GTN note (cost vs quality with expected lift) and propose a canary routing flag if the A/B supports it. Sara, you ok to try the per-channel patch and a prefix-KV toggled run?

sara: Yup — I'll run a microbench with per-channel scaling + prefix-KV enabled and post results in this thread.

dev-bot: deploy-bot: Canary created for int6-hybrid routing flag -> deploy 3289998900

ops: :thumbsup:

aj: Action items recap: liam = run A/B (24h), sara = per-channel + kv microbench, aj = GTN note + routing flag draft. We'll reconvene after the 24h window with numbers.
